title: Etale invariance of the nodal completed local ring on a curve
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $C$ be a locally finite type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] of pure dimension one [def-weil-pure-dimension], and let $e:D\to C$ be etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. For any point $y\in D$ with image $x=e(y)$, the completed local $k$-algebra $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{C,x}$ is isomorphic to $k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ if and only if $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{D,y}$ is isomorphic to $k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Whenever either condition holds, both $x$ and $y$ are closed points [def-weil-closed-points]. The completions are with respect to the maximal ideals of the indicated local rings. No separatedness, global finite type or quasi-compactness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0C57, lemma-node-etale-local; section-nodal completed-local-algebra definition over an algebraically closed field. The arbitrary-point formulation includes the automatic closedness forced by the residue k of the displayed completed k-algebra.

proof.text: Assume $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{C,x}\cong k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ as $k$-algebras. The nodal ring is local with maximal ideal $(u,v)$ and residue field $k$ (as a $k$-algebra). The local ring $\mathcal O_{C,x}$ is Noetherian, being a localization of a finitely generated $k$-algebra on an affine open of $C$ (Hilbert basis theorem; Mathlib's locally Noetherian instance for schemes locally of finite type over a field). Hence [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring] applies: the canonical $k$-algebra map $\mathcal O_{C,x}\to\widehat{\mathcal O}_{C,x}$ induces an isomorphism of residue fields, so $k\to\kappa(x)$ is an isomorphism. Apply [lem-trf-etale-completed-local-ring-iso] to this $k$-algebra isomorphism $\kappa(x)\cong k$: it makes $x$ and $y$ closed, identifies $\kappa(x)$ with $\kappa(y)$, and identifies the completed local rings. Transporting the displayed ring isomorphism across that completion isomorphism gives $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{D,y}\cong k[[u,v]]/(uv)$. Both points are closed.

source.place: Tag 0C57, lemma-node-etale-local, using the nodal completed-local-algebra definition and Tag 039M after the residue-field/closed-point reduction

proof.text: Conversely, assume $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{D,y}\cong k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ as $k$-algebras. The local ring $\mathcal O_{D,y}$ is Noetherian, $D$ being locally of finite type over $k$ (etale morphisms are locally of finite presentation, and compositions of morphisms locally of finite type are locally of finite type). The same completion-residue-field argument using [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring] gives that $k\to\kappa(y)$ is an isomorphism. Apply [lem-trf-etale-completed-local-ring-iso] in its second case: $x$ and $y$ are closed, $\kappa(x)\to\kappa(y)$ is an isomorphism, and the completed local rings are isomorphic. Transporting the nodal presentation back along this isomorphism gives $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{C,x}\cong k[[u,v]]/(uv)$. Thus the two conditions are equivalent and either one implies closedness of both points.
